playwright-cli's command names, and what they run here (each says so the first time):

  tab-list               tab
  tab-new                tab new [url]
  tab-select             tab <index>, by index only
  tab-close              tab close [url-part], or tab <index> then tab close
  open                   tab new [url] (goto <url> navigates); --mobile, --device=<name>: emulate mobile
  close                  modes off --mine; tabs stay open; lists the files you wrote
  go-back                back
  mousemove              mouse move <x> <y>
  mousedown              mouse down [button]
  mouseup                mouse up [button]
  mousewheel             mouse wheel <dx> <dy>
  go-forward             forward
  find                   snapshot --grep <text>
  dialog-accept          dialog accept [text]
  dialog-dismiss         dialog dismiss
  resize                 viewport <w>x<h>
  cookie-list            cookies
  localstorage-list      storage
  set-color-scheme       emulate dark|light
  clear-color-scheme     emulate dark off
  network-state-set      network off|on
  route-list             route
  unroute                route off <glob>|--all
  request                body <#>, the response body only
  response-body          body <#>
  video-start            record on [file.webm|file.mp4]; --filename=<file> is the file
  video-stop             record off [file]
  localstorage-get       eval localStorage.getItem("<key>")
  localstorage-set       eval localStorage.setItem("<key>", "<value>")
  localstorage-delete    eval localStorage.removeItem("<key>")
  localstorage-clear     eval localStorage.clear()
  sessionstorage-get     eval sessionStorage.getItem("<key>")
  sessionstorage-set     eval sessionStorage.setItem("<key>", "<value>")
  sessionstorage-delete  eval sessionStorage.removeItem("<key>")
  sessionstorage-clear   eval sessionStorage.clear()
  sessionstorage-list    eval Object.keys(sessionStorage)
  tracing-start          capture on, which records requests and console messages together
  tracing-stop           capture off, which prints what it recorded
  recording-start        watch on, which records the steps taken in the tab (as steps, not code)
  recording-stop         watch off, then watch, which shows the steps

Not here as such:
  run-code: eval <JavaScript> runs in the page; cdp <method> <json> sends a CDP command
  list: pw-repl where says which REPL is running; one REPL serves everyone using its browser
  attach: pw-repl serve connects to the browser on PW_CDP_URL; pw-repl skill has the rest
  detach: pw-repl stop, or quit at the prompt, disconnects and leaves the browser running
  drop, webmcp-list, webmcp-call: not here yet
  pdf: not here yet; screenshot --full-page saves the whole page as a PNG
  generate-locator: not here yet; a snapshot ref (e5) works as a selector in any command
  cookie-get: not here yet; cookies lists them without values, and cdp Network.getCookies {} shows the
      values
  cookie-set: not here yet; cdp Network.setCookie {"name": ..., "value": ..., "url": ...} sets one
  cookie-delete: not here yet; cdp Network.deleteCookies {"name": ..., "url": ...} deletes one
  show: not here; pw-repl attach, or the REPL's pane, shows everything the REPL does
  close-all: not here on purpose: it would close a browser someone else may be using; close turns off your
      modes
  kill-all: not here on purpose: it would kill a browser someone else may be using; pw-repl stop stops a
      REPL
  delete-data: not here on purpose: it would wipe the data of a browser someone else may be using
  cookie-clear: not here on purpose: it clears every site's cookies, in a browser someone else may be
      using
  state-save: not here on purpose: it would save the sign-ins of someone else sharing the browser
  state-load: not here on purpose: it would replace the sign-ins of someone else sharing the browser
  install: not needed here: pw-repl needs no workspace set up; pw-repl skill says how to use it
  install-browser: not needed here: --launch uses Playwright's Chromium or one on the PATH (PW_CHROME)
  set-reduced-motion, clear-reduced-motion, set-forced-colors, clear-forced-colors, set-contrast,
      clear-contrast, set-media, clear-media: not here yet; emulate dark|light sets the color scheme
  request-headers, response-headers, request-body: not here yet; body <#> shows the response body
  video-chapter: not here: toast <text> --duration=3s shows a title over the page instead, in the video
  video-show-actions: not here; cursor on draws a pointer that moves to each action, without labels
  video-hide-actions: not here; cursor off hides the pointer cursor on draws
  pause-at, resume, step-over: not here: they step through a Playwright test

Names both have (goto, click, fill, snapshot, eval, ...) take playwright-cli's forms too: click <ref>
[button] [--modifiers=<keys>], fill and type --submit, type <text> into what has focus, eval <function>
<ref>, press in any case, screenshot <ref> --full-page --filename=<file>, console <level>, requests
--static --filter=<regexp>, find --regex <regexp>, route <pattern> --status= --body= --content-type=.
Its other options are refused, never read as part of a selector or a value.

Different on purpose, since the browser may be someone else's too:
  routes, network and emulation     per tab, not the whole browser, so other users' tabs are untouched
  close                             turns off your modes; tabs stay open (tab close <url-part> closes one)
  upload <selector> <file>          names the input: file pickers are not caught, as the user's would be
  no snapshot after each command    the user reads the pane too; snapshot when you need one
  -s=<session>                      -c <name> is the nearest: a client with a selected tab of its own
